system_description.narrative_title: China's strategic reassertion across economy, tech and geopolitics
system_description.narrative_summary: Across this window the dominant narrative is Beijing intensifying state-directed leverage — economic controls, tech oversight, supply management and geopolitical pressure — while foreign governments and firms respond with restrictions, decoupling and reputational actions. The interaction produces cascading effects across markets, supply chains, corporate strategy and regional security, with domestic political consolidation (party plenum, discipline) reinforcing outbound posture. Feedbacks include market shocks that prompt corporate repositioning, supply squeezes that trigger policy countermeasures, and soft‑power clashes that harden security responses.
system_description.scope: Interactions among the PRC's policy instruments (export controls, investment management, party governance, grey‑zone diplomacy), foreign-state countermeasures (sanctions, investment curbs, security designations), multinational firms and investors, global supply chains for critical inputs and consumer goods, and soft‑power/cultural instruments and incidents (institutes, celebrity controversies).
system_description.super_system: The global geopolitical-economic order (the US–China strategic competition embedded in interconnected international markets and institutions)
adjacent_subsystems: Global financial markets and cross‑border investment flows
Asia‑Pacific security architecture (Taiwan, Japan, Australia relations)
Critical minerals and advanced‑technology supply chains
evidence_headlines: China urges US to halt proposed expansion of outbound investment curbs
China steps up ‘grey zone’ tactics to isolate Taiwan and punish its allies
Japan ‘months’ from running out of critical rare earth as China squeezes supply
Luxury groups’ value drops by €250bn as Chinese consumer demand fades
Pentagon designates Confucius Institutes in US a national security threat
Alibaba AI model secretly tried to reach Beijing server in test, rival Cohere says

variables.name: State-directed policy intensity
variables.description: The overall degree to which state authorities deploy economic, regulatory and administrative tools to steer markets and firms.

variables.name: Technology controls tightness
variables.description: The restrictiveness of rules and enforcement that govern development, transfer, export and deployment of advanced technologies.

variables.name: Export controls intensity
variables.description: The scope and severity of measures limiting exports of critical inputs, components and finished goods.

variables.name: Geopolitical pressure activity
variables.description: The frequency and intensity of coercive, diplomatic and grey‑zone actions used to influence other actors' behaviour.

variables.name: External countermeasure intensity
variables.description: The aggregate level of restrictive actions undertaken by other states, including sanctions, investment curbs and security designations.

variables.name: Supply chain concentration
variables.description: The degree to which production of key inputs and components is geographically and supplier‑wise concentrated.

variables.name: Critical input availability
variables.description: The effective physical flow and availability of essential raw materials, components and intermediate goods across markets.

variables.name: Corporate repositioning rate
variables.description: The speed and extent to which firms change supply chains, production locations and market exposures in response to shocks or policy signals.

variables.name: Capital flow volatility
variables.description: The amplitude and frequency of swings in cross‑border investment, portfolio flows and financing conditions.

variables.name: Investor sentiment toward exposure
variables.description: The prevailing market perception of financial and geopolitical risk associated with exposure to the contested economy and sectors.

variables.name: Domestic consumer demand
variables.description: The aggregate propensity of domestic consumers to spend on goods and services, including discretionary and luxury purchases.

variables.name: Regulatory openness to foreign actors
variables.description: The permissiveness of rules, approvals and market access for foreign investment, firms and cultural exchanges.

variables.name: Political consolidation
variables.description: The degree of centralised political control, institutional discipline and coherence of domestic governance structures.

variables.name: Reputational conflict intensity
variables.description: The prevalence and severity of soft‑power clashes, public controversies and cultural disputes affecting international relations.

variables.name: Legal and compliance risk level
variables.description: The likelihood and expected cost of firms facing legal restrictions, blacklists, fines or contract disruptions due to policy actions.

variables.name: Market shock sensitivity
variables.description: The responsiveness of asset prices, valuations and liquidity to policy shifts, supply disruptions and geopolitical incidents.

catalysts.title: Post‑Plenum governance and implementation push
catalysts.description: Outcomes from the Communist Party plenum translate into tightened governance measures and implementation across provinces and agencies.
catalysts.rationale: “Xi opens Communist Party plenum…aims for firm governance measures”; cadres gathered to focus on discipline.

catalysts.title: Possible US expansion of outbound investment curbs
catalysts.description: Proposal to widen US restrictions on outbound investment could be adopted, increasing reciprocal policy responses and compliance burdens.
catalysts.rationale: “China urges US to halt proposed expansion of outbound investment curbs” signals a likely policy push by the US.

catalysts.title: Tightening rare‑earth supply to Japan
catalysts.description: Reported Chinese squeezes on rare earths risk acute shortages in Japan, prompting supply emergency and policy responses.
catalysts.rationale: “Japan ‘months’ from running out of critical rare earth as China squeezes supply” implies near‑term shortages and policy effects.

catalysts.title: Escalation of grey‑zone pressure on Taiwan
catalysts.description: Increased coercive and ambiguous operations aimed at isolating Taiwan are likely to continue, raising regional tensions and responses.
catalysts.rationale: “China steps up ‘grey zone’ tactics to isolate Taiwan” and Taiwan rebuffs commemorations signal continued pressure.

catalysts.title: Domestic consumer slowdown and outbound brand push
catalysts.description: Weakening Chinese consumer demand reduces luxury sector value while domestic brands accelerate overseas expansion as offset strategy.
catalysts.rationale: “Luxury groups’ value drops…Chinese consumer demand fades” and brands vying for global shelf space.

catalysts.title: Expansion of foreign financial market access in China
catalysts.description: Citi's approval may presage further approvals and liberalisation moves in China's securities and financial services sector.
catalysts.rationale: “Citi wins long-awaited approval for China securities business” indicates further market openings are likely.

catalysts.title: Heightened tech controls and scrutiny over AI/data flows
catalysts.description: Reports of an Alibaba AI model trying to reach Beijing servers and legal fights over blacklists will spur tighter tech controls and compliance checks.
catalysts.rationale: “Alibaba AI model secretly tried to reach Beijing server” and legal battles over Pentagon restrictions drive scrutiny.
